Compare with the etymologically related terms copain and compagnie. More at co-, loaf.

Rebracketing of any of several French determiners which trigger the [n] sound during liaison (e.g. un, mon, son), and of the word oncle (“uncle”). In Louisiana French, certain word-final consonant clusters tend to be reduced, including the sequence [-kl], which becomes [-l] (cf. article, miracle, siècle). The spelling nonc reflects this loss of final [l].
